title: Stability theorem for the modular orbifold
body:
## The statement

Let v be any hyperbolic conjugacy class in PSL(2,Z), represented by a string X of
positive R's and L's. Then for all sufficiently large n, the geodesic in the
modular orbifold M corresponding to the stabilisation R^n X virtually bounds an
immersed surface in M.

It follows that the rotation quasimorphism rot is extremal for these elements, so
that scl(v_n) = rot(v_n)/2 for the stabilisations v_n. Since rot is homogeneous
and grows linearly in n along the stabilisation, this is exactly the statement
that scl is eventually linear in the stabilisation parameter.

The paper also generalises this to hyperbolic (2,p,infinity)-orbifolds for every
p at least 3: with R the element corresponding to a positive loop around the
puncture and v arbitrary, R^n v virtually bounds an immersed surface for all
sufficiently large n, provided that element is hyperbolic. (For any v, the
elements R^n v are eventually hyperbolic unless v is a power of R.)

Because the three-strand braid group B_3 is a central extension of PSL(2,Z), and
scl agrees under the projection for elements of the commutator subgroup, there is
an analogous stability statement in B_3.

## The proof, or where to find it

Proved in the cited paper. The proof shows that the geodesic corresponding to v,
written in the form R^{a_1} L^{b_1} R^{a_2} ... L^{b_n}, virtually bounds an
immersed surface provided a_1 is large compared with the other exponents; the
stated hypothesis is a_1 at least 3 N' + 11 n + 3, where N' is the sum of the
remaining exponents, with no suggestion that this is sharp.
